output.title: Video-on-demand pipeline
output.description: An invented creator video platform, Lumen Studio. Uploads start an ingest workflow that fans out 4K, HD and audio encodes to queues, where KEDA scales encoders on depth; packaging fetches DRM keys and publishes HLS and DASH. Viewers stream through a CDN whose route table sends almost every segment to the edge cache.

nodes.label: Encode triage
nodes.sublabel: flag the upload, tell the creator

simulations.title: Premiere day: where the encode time goes
simulations.description: A studio delivers a festival slate: masters arrive six times faster for six seconds. Each becomes three encode jobs; KEDA adds 4K and HD encoders on queue depth. Hover the encoders and the packager for sampled p50, p95 and p99: the spike doubles them, and the growth is waiting, not encoding. Teaching timings: 1 s polling, 2 s startup.

action.text: Each master lands in Originals; an S3 event starts the ingest workflow, which fans out one job per rendition ladder.
The slate arrives: six masters a second. A 4K encode takes two seconds, so jobs wait while KEDA adds encoders.
Hover 4K encoders: p95 has doubled to about five seconds. An encode still takes two; the rest is waiting for an encoder.
Packaging fetches content keys under the DRM service's 40-a-second limit and publishes each title.

simulations.title: A batch of corrupt sources
simulations.description: A creator's export tool writes broken 4K masters for twenty seconds. Those encode jobs fail three times and go to the dead-letter queue; triage flags each upload and emails its creator. HD and audio renditions are unaffected.

action.text: Uploads arrive steadily; three ladders encode each one independently.
A batch of 4K masters is corrupt. The 4K encoder fails them; SQS makes each visible again for a retry.
After three receives a job goes to the dead-letter queue, where triage flags its upload and emails the creator.
The export tool is fixed. New 4K jobs encode again; HD and audio never stopped.

simulations.title: Premiere night: the edge cache carries it
simulations.description: The premiere goes live and viewers triple in seconds. The CDN's route table sends 97% of segment requests to the edge cache; only misses reach the origin bucket, and playback starts ask the API for a manifest and a DRM licence.

action.text: Almost every request is a video segment; a few start playback and need a manifest and a licence.
Three times the viewers. The edge cache answers 97% of segments; the origin bucket only sees misses.
Playback starts reach the API, which checks rights with the catalog and asks for a DRM licence.

expectations.label: The edge cache serves most segments
